chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon him), said:
I asked him about a man who divorced his wife three times in one sitting, or more, while she was pure (from menstruation). He said: 'It is one (divorce).'
ai.seo_question: Does pronouncing three divorces at once count as three separate divorces in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Shia jurisprudential position that simultaneous triple pronouncements constitute a single revocable divorce (talaq raj'i), contrasting with the Sunni view of immediate triple divorce. It underscores the principle that the intent and context of the pronouncement, rather than the mere count of words, determine the legal status, a key point of divergence in fiqh al-bayan. The ruling emphasizes the protective nature of divorce laws in Shia tradition, allowing for reconciliation during the waiting period (iddah).

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, and Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Jameel Bin Darraj, from Zurara,

(It has been narrated) from one of the two (5th or 6th Imam<sup>asws</sup>), said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who divorced his wife three (divorces) in one sitting, or more, and she was pure. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is one’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr from Jamil ibn Darraj from Zurarah who has said the following: “

I once asked one of the two Imam, (abu Ja‘far or abu ‘ Abd Allah), ‘Alayhim al-Salam, about the case of a man who divorces his wife three times in one place and time or [more] when she is clean of Hayd (menses). He (the Imam) said, ‘It is only one.’”
